about:
Tallapoosa River Electric Cooperative (TREC) was established in 1939 and is headquartered in LaFayette, Alabama. The cooperative operates as a not-for-profit, member-owned utility governed by a democratically elected board of trustees. It serves members across Clay, Randolph, Tallapoosa, Chambers, Lee, Russell, and Barbour counties in east-central Alabama.

TREC distributes electricity to residential, commercial, and industrial members throughout its seven-county service territory. Beyond power delivery, the cooperative provides free energy audits, free residential power quality audits, and free HVAC design assistance. It maintains multiple office locations in LaFayette, Fort Mitchell, Smith Station, Mellow Valley, and New Site, along with authorized payment drop boxes at Auburn Bank branches.

The cooperative’s members include homeowners, farmers, small businesses, and industrial facilities within its service area. TREC also supports community initiatives such as the Rural Electric Cooperative Youth Tour, which offers high school juniors scholarships and trips to Montgomery and Washington, D.C.

TREC emphasizes its not-for-profit structure and member ownership as key differentiators, with a stated motto of “providing reliable consumer service.” The organization cites commitments to integrity, innovation, accountability, community service, and fairness as guiding values.
